primary_topics: Remarks at the FEU 80th anniversary alumni reunion of former FEU Central Student Organization (FEUCSO) presidents, November 8, 2007
CJP's personal FEU arc: offered UP scholarship but couldn't afford the bus fare; enrolled at FEU; became youngest and first sophomore FEUCSO president; met Dean Salonga; met Leni

The Salonga things-money-cannot-buy teaching: 'It is good to have the things that money can buy, but first and foremost, we must aspire for the things that money cannot buy, like integrity, dignity, honor, ethics and credibility'
The jurist-vs-leader tension: CJP's claim that the qualities needed for each sometimes clash -- yet FEU gave him both the law (from the FEU Institute of Law) and the leadership (from the FEUCSO)
sub_topics: FEU Hymn quoted: 'In thy happy halls, our young hearts saw the light. Though far from home, our feet may roam; our love will still be true. Our voices shall unite, to praise thy name anew; we'll treasure within our hearts the FEU.'

Transcending ordinariness: 'for all of us who have graced the halls of the FEUCSO, there is something special that we have learned that no school can academically teach. We were sharpened in the battlefield of life, as our leadership skills were honed in our extra-curricular activities.'

The bus fare barrier: as an honor student at Mapa High with a UP scholarship, CJP couldn't afford the 15-centavo ride to Diliman; enrolled at FEU Institute of Arts and Sciences; 'I forgot my initial ambition to enter UP and continued on to the FEU Institute of Law where I met the then young and brilliant Dean Jovito R. Salonga'

Salonga's FEU-UP-Harvard-Yale education: 'Dean Salonga finished his law degree from UP, his master's from Harvard, and his doctorate in law from Yale. From him, I learned not only FEU education but also UP, Harvard and Yale erudition all combined in one law course.'

Salonga's greatest teaching (variant): 'It is good to have the things that money can buy, but first and foremost, we must aspire for the things that money cannot buy, like integrity, dignity, honor, ethics and credibility' -- note: adds 'credibility' to the standard list
NUSP and true student activism: NUSP was able to 'entice the many elite and cloistered Catholic schools to join national student activities for the first time in history'

Meeting Leni: 'in the midst of these student leadership activities that I met the editor of the Scholastican, the student organ of St. Scholastica's College. She is the sweet and charming Elenita A. Carpio who later became known as Mrs. Leni Carpio Panganiban, the light of my life.'

Jurist-and-leader tension: 'to be a jurist, one must be prepared to be a loner, to be an individualist... A jurist is a recluse, cold, stoic, unreachable, unfathomable. On the other hand, a leader is an incandescent team player who is versed in people skills; a consensus builder who systematically delegates authority and responsibility.' -- 'I learned the basics of the law from the FEU Institute of Law, and the fundamentals of leadership from the FEUCSO.'

CJP's claim that FEU gave him BOTH -- the law from the Institute of Law and leadership from the FEUCSO -- is the governing institutional thesis of this speech.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 8, 2007 at the FEU 80th anniversary alumni reunion of former FEUCSO (FEU Central Student Organization) presidents, this address by CJP opens by congratulating FEU, Chair Lourdes Reyes Montinola and President Lydia Echauz, quoting the FEU Hymn ('In thy happy halls, our young hearts saw the light'), and noting that FEUCSO alumni 'transcended the call of ordinariness as we climbed the heights of student leadership' through extra-curricular activities 'that no school can academically teach.' His FEU arc: offered a UP scholarship as an honor Mapa High graduate but couldn't afford the 15-centavo bus fare to Diliman; enrolled at FEU; was 'immediately thrown into the vortex of extra-curricular activities' and forgot his UP ambition; continued to the FEU Institute of Law where he met 'the then young and brilliant Dean Jovito R. Salonga.' Salonga's unique pedagogical synthesis: 'from him, I learned not only FEU education but also UP, Harvard and Yale erudition all combined in one law course.' Salonga's governing teaching (with 'credibility' added): 'It is good to have the things that money can buy, but first and foremost, we must aspire for the things that money cannot buy, like integrity, dignity, honor, ethics and credibility.' Through NUSP, he was able to entice elite Catholic schools to join national student activities 'for the first time in history' -- and 'in the midst of these student leadership activities, I met the editor of the Scholastican, the student organ of St. Scholastica's College. She is the sweet and charming Elenita A. Carpio who later became known as Mrs. Leni Carpio Panganiban, the light of my life.' The jurist-vs-leader tension: 'a jurist is a recluse, cold, stoic, unreachable, unfathomable. A leader is an incandescent team player who is versed in people skills; a consensus builder.' CJP's synthesis: 'I learned the basics of the law from the FEU Institute of Law, and the fundamentals of leadership from the FEUCSO.' Closes: 'Let us all stand, my brothers and sisters in the FEUCSO, and proclaim our fidelity to the home of achievers and leaders! Mabuhay ang FEU!'
